testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: The new `[...new Set(...)]` dedupe in closingRefusals' ownTickets is not covered by any test. Removing it leaves all 143 dispatch tests green. The case it guards is a PR whose settled `impl-N=PR#` token and claim-branch ticket name the same ticket and whose body does not close it. Without the dedupe, that case emits two identical 'does not close #N' failure lines.
survived.evidence: Mutant B replaced `const ownTickets = [...new Set(claim === null ? tickets : [...tickets, Number(claim[1])])];` with `const ownTickets = claim === null ? tickets : [...tickets, Number(claim[1])];`. red: n/a (mutant survived). Mutant run: ./agent-test tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs → exit 0, tests 143, pass 143, fail 0. Baseline: same command → exit 0, tests 143, pass 143. Mutants A, C and D under the same command went red with 3, 2 and 1 failures respectively, so the harness does discriminate.
survived.suggested_fix: Add a test with a settled token `impl-3545=PR#3606` (a row with the token), head `implementer/3545-impl-3545` and a body closing nothing. Assert the refusal names `does not close #3545` exactly once, for example by counting matches in the refusal text.

unverified.claim: The rewritten comment above the finisher-pr block in runDispatch has a stray line break ('no closing / reference may be its own / suggestion-band record ...'), which leaves one short line in a paragraph whose other lines are filled to width; this is cosmetic only and changes no behaviour.
unverified.evidence: `sed -n 2449,2457p` on the copy's plugin/scripts/ledger.mjs (via the grep context output) shows line 2452 as '  // reference may be its own' between full-width lines 2451 and 2453.
unverified.suggested_fix: Re-wrap lines 2451-2455 into evenly filled lines.

unverified.claim: No logic error, missed case or scope creep was found. Every behaviour change matches the #4229 brief, and both mutants of the new check-1 logic are caught by the PR's tests.
unverified.evidence: Baseline in the copy, `env -u FORCE_COLOR node --test tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs tests/ledger-settle-report.test.mjs`: tests 221, pass 221, fail 0. M1 (m1/ledger.mjs:2192 `for (const n of tickets)`, which drops the claim-branch ticket from check 1) gave 'fail 2 / pass 141' on ledger-dispatch. It was caught by 'an inherited PR headed by a claim branch is refused while its body does not close that claim's ticket...' and by '...closes that claim's in-progress ticket and is dispatched...'. M2 (m2/ledger.mjs:2192 `for (const n of [])`, which removes check 1) gave 'fail 14 / pass 129'. That includes the observed-case test 'an implementer PR must close its own ticket whatever its ruling' (rule no and yes), the blank-verdict 'any row for the PR passes the ruling...' test and the two-token test. The brief's test list (cases 1 to 5, the two tests that gain a check-1 line, and the deleted blank-verdict and re-ruling tests) corresponds one-to-one to the diff's test hunks. The CLAIM_BRANCH back-reference makes 'implementer/3545-impl-3546' a non-claim head, so its own ticket is null, as that test expects.

unverified.claim: The diff introduces no swallowed errors, no new try/catch, and no dereference moved inside an existing try. One semantic widening is by design: the "ruling" gate is now satisfied by any row naming the PR, including a row whose two verdict columns are both blank, which tier-outcomes.mjs treats as never ruled. The refusal text still says the PR "has no ruling", although a row that was never ruled now passes.
unverified.evidence: rulingOf's only try/catch still wraps just readFileSync and parseTierOutcomes, and still dies loudly with the file name. `rows.some(...)` sits outside the try, as `rows.findLast(...)` did before. parseTierOutcomes (tier-outcomes.mjs 180-201) still throws on a malformed width or verdict, so a corrupt row is refused, not passed. The new test "any row for the PR passes the ruling, whatever its date, width or verdicts…" dispatches on a both-blank row. The row-existence check was already how the old gate worked; the diff only stops reading its verdicts. closingRefusals' new `CLAIM_BRANCH.exec(view.headRefName)` is safe, because prView already dies unless headRefName is a string. The new own-ticket check fails loudly: it pushes a failure line, and the dispatch dies naming PR and ticket.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: reword the "has no ruling" refusal to "has no tier-outcomes row", since the gate checks row existence only.

unverified.claim: The gh stub now accepts `issue view N --json title,labels` through an extra `||` alternative. The settle-report suite was only adjusted so finisher dispatches pass the new own-ticket gate, and nothing there asserts a missing-ticket refusal.
unverified.evidence: Diff lines 453-454 and the `closingOwnTicket` helper (diff 471-476). The edit only widens the stub's accepted argument list. All 221 tests in the two touched suites pass in my copy.
unverified.suggested_fix: None required; the refusal paths are covered in ledger-dispatch.test.mjs.

unverified.claim: The rulingOf() header comment this diff adds says 'the row's verdicts are read by nothing here', but parseTierOutcomes(), which rulingOf() calls, reads every verdict cell. It throws on a non-yes/no value, or on exactly one blank verdict, and rulingOf() turns that throw into a refusal. Not every row passes: a malformed-verdict row still blocks the finisher.
unverified.evidence: ledger.mjs:1999-2006 is the new comment ('Any row passes, whatever its date or verdicts ... the row's verdicts are read by nothing here'). tier-outcomes.mjs:180-198 is parseTierOutcomes, which throws 'malformed row: closed_own_ticket is ... expected yes, no or blank' and 'expected both blank or both yes or no'. The rulingOf() catch returns the refusal 'cannot read the PR's ruling off ...'.
unverified.suggested_fix: Say that no verdict decides the gate, but a row with a malformed verdict cell still fails parseTierOutcomes() and refuses. Or drop the added clause.

unverified.claim: The diff re-wrapped the runDispatch comment badly. It now breaks mid-clause, with 'no closing reference may be its own' alone on one line and 'suggestion-band record ...' starting the next. The text is accurate but ragged, which is cosmetic.
unverified.evidence: ledger.mjs:2449-2457: lines read '// PR must close its own tickets, whatever its ruling, and no closing', '// reference may be its own', '// suggestion-band record or a ticket another claim holds, and the PR must'.

unverified.claim: rulingOf() no longer returns or reads a ruling. It now returns only {tickets, refusal}, but the name and its callers still call it a ruling (`const ruled = await rulingOf(...)`). The shape is an untyped object literal built in four return sites. Nothing stops a caller from reading the removed `ruling` or `tsv` fields, and that would give `undefined` silently.
unverified.evidence: The grep found one caller (ledger.mjs:2467 `ruled = await rulingOf(member.number)`). It uses only ruled.refusal, ruled.tickets, and passes `ruled` to closingRefusals({tickets}). The diff removes `ruling` and `tsv` from every return. No other readers of those fields turned up in plugin/scripts.
unverified.suggested_fix: Rename it to something like rulingGate(), or return a frozen object whose shape is documented once. The `refusal: string|null` and `tickets` fields are already documented in the comment, so a rename is enough.

unverified.claim: The invariant that a PR closes its own tickets is now enforced by a runtime loop over ownTickets. The ownTickets set is built once and reused by check 3, so the two checks cannot drift apart. The cast `Number(claim[1])` is safe: CLAIM_BRANCH's capture group is `[1-9][0-9]*`, so it always yields a positive integer, and it matches the numeric `refs` entries compared with includes. No conformance-erasing cast is introduced.
unverified.evidence: stranded.mjs:209 `CLAIM_BRANCH = /^implementer\/([1-9][0-9]*)-(impl-\1(?:-[a-z])?)$/`. The diff builds `ownTickets = [...new Set(claim === null ? tickets : [...tickets, Number(claim[1])])]` and uses it in both check 1 and claimedElsewhere().

unverified.claim: closingRefusals destructures a one-field object `{ tickets }` from rulingOf()'s whole answer now that `ruling` and `tsv` are gone; passing `ruled.tickets` directly removes the object indirection and matches labelRefusal(member, tickets, refs), the sibling call two lines below.
unverified.evidence: Single caller found by grep `closingRefusals` in plugin/scripts/*.mjs: ledger.mjs:2469 `closingRefusals(member, ruled)`. In a scratch copy I changed line 2182 to `async function closingRefusals(member, tickets) {` and line 2469 to `const closing = await closingRefusals(member, ruled.tickets);`; `node --check plugin/scripts/ledger.mjs` passed and `node --test tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs tests/ledger-settle-report.test.mjs` → exit=0, ℹ tests 221, ℹ pass 221, ℹ fail 0.
unverified.suggested_fix: async function closingRefusals(member, tickets) { … } and at the call site: const closing = await closingRefusals(member, ruled.tickets);

unverified.claim: The test 'a PR is refused while its body does not close its ticket, and recorded once it does' (3606/3545, default ruling yes, closes nothing → refused 'does not close #3545, its own ticket', then closes [3545] → dispatched) duplicates the new 'an implementer PR must close its own ticket whatever its ruling' test's `closed = "yes"` iteration, which runs the same sequence with a stricter anchored regex plus a dispatched-list assertion.
unverified.evidence: Read snapshot tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs 1575-1583 and 1598-1609 side by side: same steps (put row, rule with verdict yes, refused with 'does not close #N, its own ticket — add "Closes #N" to its body', dispatched == [], closes(bin, pr, [N]), ok → fleet-finisher); the 4072 test additionally asserts no 'closed_own_ticket' in the message and dispatched == ['finisher-pr-4072']. The 'any row for the PR passes the ruling…' test at 1488 covers the same refuse-then-close path a third time. Not executed as a mutation-kill comparison — subsumption is from reading.
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete the 1575 test (or the 'yes' iteration's overlap) and keep the 4072 loop as the single owner of the 'must close its own ticket' refuse-then-dispatch behavior.
